lessons.title: From France to Nuevo León
lessons.subtitle: Gignac’s route to Tigres crossed three French clubs.

story.title: A French start
story.body: He made his first-division debut with Lorient in 2006–07.

story.title: The next step
story.body: He then played for Toulouse and Marseille before joining Tigres in 2015.

lessons.title: The 200th goal
lessons.subtitle: A January night in León marked Gignac’s two-hundredth official Tigres goal.

story.title: A milestone away
story.body: On January 17, 2024, Gignac scored in the 76th minute against León.

story.title: A dated benchmark
story.body: Tigres identified that strike as Gignac’s 200th official club goal. Its breakdown lists 175 in the league and liguilla, with the remaining goals spread across other competitions.

lessons.title: Goals with discipline
lessons.subtitle: A club retrospective noted both longevity and a rare disciplinary record.

story.title: A snapshot, not a live count
story.body: In a 2020 retrospective, Tigres described Gignac’s first-division career and noted that he had not received a red card through that article’s publication.

story.title: The lasting record
story.body: The date matters: this is a dated snapshot.

lessons.title: Two goals in a comeback
lessons.subtitle: Gignac helped Tigres turn around a Concacaf tie against Alianza.

story.title: A difficult first half
story.body: On February 26, 2020, Tigres beat Alianza 4–2 and advanced 5–4 on aggregate.

story.title: The defining moment
story.body: Gignac scored twice during the home leg.

lessons.title: The keeper from Rosario
lessons.subtitle: Nahuel Guzmán’s path ran from Newell’s to San Nicolás de los Garza.

story.title: Home club and loan
story.body: Nahuel developed and made his professional debut at Newell’s Old Boys.

story.title: The next step
story.body: After a loan at Independiente Rivadavia and a return to Newell’s, he joined Tigres for Apertura 2014.

lessons.title: A goalkeeper’s last-minute header
lessons.subtitle: Nahuel became the unlikely scorer who kept Tigres alive in a continental tie.

story.title: A leap in stoppage time
story.body: With Tigres trailing in the two-leg series, Nahuel headed home at minute 93 against Alianza on February 26, 2020.

story.title: The defining moment
story.body: The 4–2 win sent Tigres through 5–4 on aggregate.

lessons.title: Five hundred Tigres matches
lessons.subtitle: A quarterfinal in Aguascalientes marked a club appearance record.

story.title: A landmark at Necaxa
story.body: Nahuel reached 500 official Tigres appearances in the away leg against Necaxa during the Clausura 2025 quarterfinals.

story.title: A dated benchmark
story.body: In its 11 May 2025 account, Tigres identified him as its all-time appearance leader. Of his first 500 matches, 411 were in the league and liguilla; the remainder were in other competitions.

lessons.title: Across eight competitions
lessons.subtitle: Nahuel’s milestone total came from a wide range of tournaments.

story.title: A broad workload
story.body: At 500 official games in May 2025, most of Nahuel’s appearances were in Mexico’s first division.

story.title: The next step
story.body: His remaining matches came across continental, regional and global competitions.

lessons.title: The first league crown
lessons.subtitle: Rayados overturned a first-leg deficit to earn a long-awaited championship.

story.title: A comeback in Mexico 86
story.body: Monterrey lost the first final leg 2–1, then beat Tampico Madero 2–0 on March 1, 1986.

story.title: The decisive detail
story.body: The 3–2 aggregate result delivered the club’s first league title.

lessons.title: Three continental crowns in a row
lessons.subtitle: Monterrey built a Concacaf dynasty before winning the title again in 2019.

story.title: A regional run
story.body: Rayados won the Concacaf title in 2011, 2012 and 2013.

story.title: The next era
story.body: The 2019 victory over Tigres was their fourth, and the first continental final between the city rivals.

lessons.title: The first continental Clásico Regio
lessons.subtitle: The city rivalry became a continental final in 2019.

story.title: A narrow aggregate win
story.body: Monterrey took a 1–0 first-leg lead into the return match.

story.title: The decisive detail
story.body: A 1–1 draw at home made the aggregate 2–1 and secured the Concacaf trophy.

lessons.title: A Chilean striker finds a home in Monterrey
lessons.subtitle: Suazo’s path to Rayados ran through Chile and Spain.

story.title: Before and after Rayados
story.body: Suazo began his professional career with Audax Italiano and became a prolific scorer at Colo-Colo.

story.title: The next step
story.body: He joined Monterrey in 2007 and later spent part of 2010 with Zaragoza.

lessons.title: A scoring crown in his first full season
lessons.subtitle: Suazo turned a standout Clausura into a club record.

story.title: A memorable spring
story.body: In the Clausura 2008, Suazo scored 13 goals to win the league’s scoring crown.

story.title: The defining moment
story.body: His four-goal performance against Veracruz was another landmark in that campaign.

lessons.title: A long Rayados chapter
lessons.subtitle: The striker’s two spells at Monterrey framed a decorated run.

story.title: Leave and return
story.body: After joining in 2007, Suazo spent the first half of 2010 with Zaragoza.

story.title: The next step
story.body: He returned to Monterrey and remained through December 2014 before leaving for Colo-Colo.

lessons.title: A record that lasted
lessons.subtitle: Suazo’s name became the standard for Rayados’ scorers.

story.title: The benchmark
story.body: His 121 goals set the club scoring mark later matched by Rogelio Funes Mori in April 2021.

story.title: A dated benchmark
story.body: Suazo’s Rayados honors also include league and Concacaf titles.

lessons.title: A route across three countries
lessons.subtitle: Funes Mori arrived in Monterrey after stints in Argentina, Portugal and Turkey.

story.title: New home in 2015
story.body: Born in Mendoza, Funes Mori played for River Plate, Benfica and Eskişehirspor.

story.title: The next step
story.body: He signed for Rayados in 2015.

lessons.title: His first Rayados appearances
lessons.subtitle: Funes Mori’s first weeks brought a debut and early goals.

story.title: A summer start
story.body: Funes Mori debuted against Pumas in July 2015.

story.title: The defining moment
story.body: Three days later, he scored his first official Rayados goal against Correcaminos in the Copa MX.

lessons.title: Matching the club scoring mark
lessons.subtitle: Funes Mori caught Suazo with a goal against Atlético de San Luis.

story.title: A tie in the record book
story.body: On April 3, 2021, the striker scored his 121st Rayados goal.

story.title: A dated benchmark
story.body: That equaled the mark held by Humberto Suazo at the time.

lessons.title: A 160-goal farewell
lessons.subtitle: Funes Mori’s final Rayados season closed with a major career total.

story.title: A prolific departure
story.body: In his final match for Monterrey, on December 2, 2023, he scored against Atlético de San Luis.

story.title: The lasting record
story.body: The club’s January 2024 farewell counted 160 goals in 328 official appearances.

lessons.title: A return to the professional ranks
lessons.subtitle: The modern rise began with promotion and a landmark final.

story.title: Promotion and breakthrough
story.body: Pachuca returned to the top division in 1998.

story.title: The next era
story.body: A year later, the club won its first professional-era league championship by defeating Cruz Azul in extra time.

lessons.title: A Mexican club wins in South America
lessons.subtitle: Pachuca carried its continental success beyond Concacaf.

story.title: A rare achievement
story.body: In 2006, Pachuca defeated Colo-Colo over two legs to win the Copa Sudamericana.

story.title: The decisive detail
story.body: The club became the first Mexican side to lift a CONMEBOL-organized trophy.

lessons.title: One goal settled the Concacaf final
lessons.subtitle: Pachuca edged Tigres in the 2017 regional championship.

story.title: Jara at the decisive moment
story.body: Franco Jara scored in the 83rd minute of the second leg.

story.title: The decisive detail
story.body: Pachuca won that match 1–0 and the final 2–1 on aggregate.

lessons.title: The Colombian keeper arrives
lessons.subtitle: Miguel Calero became a central figure in Pachuca’s rise.

story.title: From Valle del Cauca to Hidalgo
story.body: Born in Ginebra, Colombia, Calero arrived at Pachuca for Invierno 2000.

story.title: The next step
story.body: He made his official debut on July 30 of that year.

lessons.title: Calero’s farewell in the Hidalgo
lessons.subtitle: The goalkeeper signed off with a clean sheet.

story.title: The last match
story.body: Pachuca’s retirement retrospective dates Calero’s farewell to 22 October 2011, in the Estadio Hidalgo.

story.title: One last clean sheet
story.body: He kept his goal unbeaten in that final appearance. This retirement moment is separate from his arrival in 2000 and the later SuperLiga penalty save.

lessons.title: A keeper among champions
lessons.subtitle: Calero collected domestic and continental trophies in Hidalgo.

story.title: A decorated captain
story.body: Pachuca credits Calero with four league titles and five international trophies.

story.title: A dated benchmark
story.body: His honours spanned Liga MX, Concacaf and the 2006 Sudamericana.

lessons.title: A penalty save against Landon Donovan
lessons.subtitle: Calero helped Pachuca win the 2007 SuperLiga final.

story.title: A shootout turning point
story.body: Pachuca beat LA Galaxy on penalties in the 2007 SuperLiga final.

story.title: The defining moment
story.body: Calero stopped Landon Donovan’s attempt before Pachuca lifted the trophy.

lessons.title: From Pachuca to Europe
lessons.subtitle: Lozano’s first senior chapter was a productive one in Hidalgo.

story.title: A young winger rises
story.body: Lozano played 149 matches for Pachuca, scoring 43 goals and recording 28 assists.

story.title: The next step
story.body: He left for Europe in July 2017.

lessons.title: A July move to Europe
lessons.subtitle: The winger left after the 2017 Concacaf triumph.

story.title: Next stop: the Netherlands
story.body: Lozano departed Pachuca in July 2017 and joined PSV Eindhoven.

story.title: The next step
story.body: He later continued his European career at Napoli.

lessons.title: Golden Boot and young-player award
lessons.subtitle: Lozano’s Concacaf campaign brought both team and individual honours.

story.title: A standout campaign
story.body: Lozano helped Pachuca win the 2016–17 Concacaf competition and finished as its top scorer with eight goals.

story.title: A dated benchmark
story.body: He also received the Best Young Player award.

lessons.title: Lozano scores on his Liga MX debut
lessons.subtitle: An Azteca breakthrough in February 2014.

story.title: A scoring introduction
story.body: On 8 February 2014, Lozano made his Liga MX debut against América at the Azteca and scored the winner.

story.title: Keep the debuts separate
story.body: He had already played in Copa MX. This lesson concerns his first Liga MX appearance, when his goal gave Pachuca a 1–0 win.

lessons.title: A Paris club is born
lessons.subtitle: A merger gave the capital a new team

story.title: A club wanted by Paris
story.body: With no Parisian side in the top division, a campaign for a major Paris club drew support from 66,000 people.

story.title: A merger made it possible
story.body: Paris Football Club joined with Stade Sangermanois. The merged club earned promotion in its first season.

lessons.title: Brussels brings a European first
lessons.subtitle: N’Gotty’s strike made history

story.title: A final in Brussels
story.body: On 8 May 1996, PSG met Rapid Vienna in the Cup Winners’ Cup final at the Stade du Roi Baudouin.

story.title: One free kick decided it
story.body: Bruno N’Gotty struck from a long-range free kick before half-time. PSG held on for a 1–0 win and its first European trophy.

lessons.title: Four past Barcelona
lessons.subtitle: A first-leg masterclass at the Parc

story.title: A fast start
story.body: On 14 February 2017, PSG overwhelmed Barcelona in the first leg of their Champions League round-of-16 tie.

story.title: Two from Di María
story.body: Ángel Di María scored twice; Julian Draxler and Edinson Cavani added one apiece in the 4–0 win.

lessons.title: A prodigy rises at Monaco
lessons.subtitle: A late-season surge helped deliver the league title

story.title: A first taste
story.body: Mbappé made his Ligue 1 debut for Monaco in December 2015. His first half-season brought 11 league appearances, one goal and one assist.

story.title: A decisive run
story.body: In 2016/17, the 17-year-old became central to Monaco’s title race. Across 13 closing matches, he scored 12 goals and assisted three, including the title-clinching goal on 17 May 2017.

lessons.title: A hat-trick at Camp Nou
lessons.subtitle: Mbappé turns the tie around

story.title: Paris responds
story.body: On 16 February 2021, Barcelona scored first at Camp Nou. Mbappé equalised before Paris took control.

story.title: Three goals away
story.body: Mbappé scored a treble in a 4–1 first-leg win. UEFA named him Player of the Match.

lessons.title: Goal 201 makes history
lessons.subtitle: A personal milestone against Nantes

story.title: A record at the Parc
story.body: On 4 March 2023, Mbappé scored his 201st PSG goal against Nantes in a 4–2 league win.

story.title: The new leading scorer
story.body: At 24 years and 2 months, he passed Edinson Cavani’s club record, reaching the mark in 247 appearances.

lessons.title: A record run of league honours
lessons.subtitle: Mbappé’s individual awards set new Ligue 1 marks

story.title: Five best-player awards
story.body: Ligue 1’s official honours list credits Mbappé with five Player of the Year awards: 2019 and four straight from 2021 through 2024.

story.title: Six scoring crowns
story.body: He became the first player to win the Ligue 1 top-scorer title six times, leading the league every season from 2019 through 2024. His PSG side also reached the 2020 Champions League final.

lessons.title: Ibrahimović joins PSG
lessons.subtitle: A transfer from Milan began four seasons in Paris

story.title: From Milan to Paris
story.body: PSG signed Ibrahimović from AC Milan on 18 July 2012. UEFA reported that the striker agreed to a three-year contract.

story.title: His longest club stay
story.body: Paris became Ibrahimović’s longest spell at one club. Ligue 1 records 180 appearances for PSG in all competitions, more than he made for any other side.

lessons.title: An immediate impact in Paris
lessons.subtitle: Ibrahimović rescued PSG on his league debut

story.title: A debut brace
story.body: Ibrahimović’s first PSG league appearance came at the Parc des Princes on 11 August 2012 against Lorient. After PSG fell two goals behind, his first Ligue 1 brace brought them back level.

story.title: A four-year run
story.body: The comeback launched a four-season Paris stay. He went on to score 113 Ligue 1 goals in 122 appearances and lead the league in scoring three times.

lessons.title: A historic scoring season
lessons.subtitle: His final Ligue 1 campaign set a personal peak

story.title: Thirty-eight goals
story.body: In 2015/16 Ibrahimović scored 38 Ligue 1 goals in 31 appearances. It was the league’s third-highest single-season total at the time.

story.title: A rare four-goal match
story.body: On 13 March 2016, he scored four times in PSG’s 9–0 win at Troyes, as the club secured the title with eight league matches remaining.

lessons.title: A final match with a brace
lessons.subtitle: Ibrahimović signed off with a Coupe de France win

story.title: A cup final farewell
story.body: Ibrahimović’s final PSG match was the Coupe de France final on 21 May 2016 against Marseille. PSG won 4–2 at the Stade de France.

story.title: A decisive finish
story.body: The Swedish striker scored twice in the final. The victory gave PSG its tenth Coupe de France, matching Marseille’s tally at the time.

lessons.title: From St Mark’s to Manchester City
lessons.subtitle: A church team evolved into a city club

story.title: A local beginning
story.body: St Mark’s Church formed a football team in 1880. That team would eventually become Manchester City.

story.title: A name for the whole city
story.body: The team became Ardwick in 1887, then reorganised as Manchester City Football Club in 1894.

lessons.title: A trophy after 35 years
lessons.subtitle: Yaya Touré’s Wembley goal ends the wait

story.title: A Wembley final
story.body: On 14 May 2011, City faced Stoke in the FA Cup final, looking to end a 35-year wait for a major trophy.

story.title: One strike settled it
story.body: Yaya Touré scored in the 74th minute for a 1–0 win. The cup began a new successful period for the club.

lessons.title: City completes the Treble
lessons.subtitle: Rodri’s strike brings a first Champions League

story.title: A first European Cup
story.body: On 10 June 2023, City faced Inter in Istanbul in its first Champions League final.

story.title: One goal was enough
story.body: Rodri scored in the second half for a 1–0 win. City completed the Treble with its first Champions League crown.

lessons.title: Agüero joins City
lessons.subtitle: An immediate impact from his debut

story.title: A new signing
story.body: Agüero joined Manchester City on 27 July 2011 after five seasons at Atlético Madrid.

story.title: A fast introduction
story.body: He made his City debut against Swansea on 15 August and scored 30 times in his first season.

lessons.title: The 93:20 winner
lessons.subtitle: Agüero turns a title race around

story.title: A late comeback
story.body: On 13 May 2012, QPR led City 2–1 late in stoppage time while City needed a win to be champions.

story.title: A decisive finish
story.body: Agüero scored at 93:20 to make it 3–2 and secure City’s first Premier League title.

lessons.title: A record City goalscorer
lessons.subtitle: His 260 goals came in 390 games

story.title: An all-time club record
story.body: Agüero finished his City career with 260 goals in 390 appearances, the club record at the time of his departure.

story.title: A Premier League mark
story.body: He also set the league record for most hat-tricks, with 12, across his City seasons.

lessons.title: A medal-winning City era
lessons.subtitle: Five league titles among his honours

story.title: A decorated spell
story.body: City lists 14 medals for Agüero: five Premier League titles, five League Cups, one FA Cup and three Community Shields.

story.title: More than a goal
story.body: The honours came during a decade in which Agüero became the club’s leading scorer and an emblem of its rise.

lessons.title: A World Cup winner arrives
lessons.subtitle: Silva joins from Valencia in 2010

story.title: From Gran Canaria
story.body: David Silva was born in Arguineguín, Gran Canaria, on 8 January 1986.

story.title: A summer move
story.body: A World Cup winner with Spain, he moved from Valencia to Manchester City in July 2010.

lessons.title: A derby remembered in passes
lessons.subtitle: Silva assists Džeko in the 6–1 win

story.title: Old Trafford, October 2011
story.body: City beat Manchester United 6–1 away in a landmark Premier League derby.

story.title: A creator’s contribution
story.body: The club later singled out Silva’s vision and execution in his assist for Edin Džeko as an example of his playmaking.

lessons.title: A decade of City appearances
lessons.subtitle: 436 games and a European milestone

story.title: A top-ten career
story.body: Silva’s 436th City appearance, against Lyon, moved him into the club’s all-time top ten in August 2020.

story.title: A European high
story.body: That Lyon match was his 70th European appearance for City, then a club record.

lessons.title: Honours across a decade
lessons.subtitle: Four Premier League titles and more

story.title: A long list of silverware
story.body: Across ten years, Silva won four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and five League Cups with City.

story.title: A lasting tribute
story.body: The club announced a statue and a training pitch mosaic to honour his contribution.

lessons.title: Athletic Club de Madrid begins
lessons.subtitle: Students start a club in 1903

story.title: A group of students
story.body: Young Basque students living in Madrid founded Athletic Club de Madrid on 26 April 1903.

story.title: A pitch by the Retiro
story.body: The club’s first field stood behind the Retiro walls; members played the first match on 2 May.

lessons.title: A title secured at Camp Nou
lessons.subtitle: Godín’s header earns the point

story.title: A final-day decider
story.body: On 17 May 2014, Atlético visited Barcelona knowing a draw would secure the league title.

story.title: A header after the break
story.body: Diego Godín rose to meet Koke’s corner. The 1–1 draw gave Atlético its tenth Spanish league championship.

lessons.title: An Intercontinental comeback
lessons.subtitle: Atlético overturns Independiente’s first-leg lead

story.title: A return at the Calderón
story.body: On 10 April 1975, Atlético hosted Independiente in the decisive second leg of the Intercontinental Cup.

story.title: Two goals turn the tie
story.body: Atlético won 2–0 after losing the first leg 1–0. Irureta scored at 21 minutes and Ayala struck at 86.

lessons.title: Torres rises from the academy
lessons.subtitle: A teenager earns his first-team place

story.title: An academy boy
story.body: Torres joined Atlético’s academy at 11 and made his senior debut against Leganés on 27 May 2001.

story.title: First goal a week later
story.body: He scored his first senior goal against Albacete seven days after his debut.

lessons.title: A farewell brace
lessons.subtitle: Torres scores twice at the Calderón goodbye

story.title: A stadium’s last match
story.body: At the Vicente Calderón farewell match, Torres scored two of Atlético’s three goals against Athletic Club.

story.title: A fitting send-off
story.body: The boy who had debuted at the ground returned to score a brace in its farewell game.

lessons.title: A century of Atlético goals
lessons.subtitle: Torres reaches 100 against Eibar

story.title: A round number
story.body: On 6 February 2016, Torres scored his 100th goal for Atlético against Eibar in a 3–1 win.

story.title: A lasting total
story.body: He ended his Atlético career with 404 appearances and 129 goals.

lessons.title: A childhood dream fulfilled
lessons.subtitle: Torres lifts the Europa League with Atleti

story.title: The final in Lyon
story.body: Torres came on late in the 2018 Europa League final as Atlético beat Marseille 3–0.

story.title: A title at last
story.body: Atlético’s retrospective says winning that trophy fulfilled the dream he had held since childhood.

lessons.title: Griezmann’s first Atleti spell
lessons.subtitle: A debut and first goal in 2014

story.title: A summer arrival
story.body: Griezmann joined Atlético ahead of the 2014/15 season and debuted in the Spanish Super Cup on 10 August 2014.

story.title: A European first
story.body: His first Atlético goal came in a Champions League match against Olympiacos in September.

lessons.title: A brace on home soil
lessons.subtitle: Griezmann’s two goals power a final win

story.title: Back in France
story.body: On 16 May 2018, Griezmann returned to France for the Europa League final against Marseille in Lyon.

story.title: Two goals, one trophy
story.body: He scored Atlético’s first two goals in a 3–0 win and was named the final’s official man of the match.

lessons.title: Level with Luis Aragonés
lessons.subtitle: 173 goals in two Atlético spells

story.title: A landmark against Getafe
story.body: On 19 December 2023, Griezmann scored twice against Getafe to draw level with Luis Aragonés on 173 Atlético goals.

story.title: The tally behind the mark
story.body: He reached that total in 364 matches across two spells, from 2014–19 and from 2021 onward.

lessons.title: Club and country honours
lessons.subtitle: A Europa League champion and World Cup winner

story.title: Success in 2018
story.body: Griezmann won the Europa League with Atlético and the World Cup with France in 2018.

story.title: Individual recognition
story.body: He finished third in the 2018 Ballon d’Or, the same year as those two major titles.

lessons.title: A rapid rise in the late 1960s
lessons.subtitle: The first trophies came soon after Cruz Azul reached the top division.

story.title: A fast ascent
story.body: In the 1960s, Cruz Azul turned promotion into a string of major titles. The league triumph in 1968–69 was followed by a domestic cup and the club’s first Concacaf trophy.

story.title: The detail behind the milestone
story.body: The chronology is clearest in first league title (1968–69) and cup final opponent (Monterrey), which anchor the wider story.

lessons.title: The blue machine of the 1970s
lessons.subtitle: Titles and a famous final made Cruz Azul the era’s defining team.

story.title: A dominant stretch
story.body: Cruz Azul added three consecutive league championships in 1971–72, 1972–73 and 1973–74. Its 1971–72 final against América became one of the club’s signature wins.

story.title: A signature final win
story.body: A 4–1 win against América at the Azteca anchored the run. Cruz Azul kept the championship through 1973–74, completing three consecutive league titles.

lessons.title: The ninth star returns
lessons.subtitle: A record-breaking regular season led to Cruz Azul’s 2021 championship.

story.title: Twelve straight wins
story.body: Cruz Azul matched a professional-era Liga MX record with 12 consecutive regular-season victories in Guard1anes 2021. The club then beat Santos 1–0 away in the first leg of the final.

story.title: The goal that brought the ninth star
story.body: On 30 May, Jonathan Rodríguez scored after Yoshimar Yotún’s pass in the return leg. That goal restored Cruz Azul’s 2–1 aggregate lead and secured its ninth league championship.

lessons.title: From an América champion to the World Cup
lessons.subtitle: Hermosillo’s career began with success at América before his great Cruz Azul chapter.

story.title: An early champion at América
story.body: In his Concacaf interview, Carlos Hermosillo recalled winning the Mexican league with Club América in 1983–84. Senior teammates helped him build the foundations of his career.

story.title: A squad place and a playing debut
story.body: Hermosillo was in Mexico’s 1986 World Cup squad but did not play. His first actual World Cup experience came at USA 1994, where Mexico topped a group containing Italy, Norway and Ireland.

lessons.title: Three consecutive scoring crowns
lessons.subtitle: A 35-goal campaign formed part of a longer scoring-title run.

story.title: A personal scoring run
story.body: Cruz Azul’s history credits Hermosillo with three consecutive league scoring titles. In the 1994–95 season, he scored 35 league goals.

story.title: A sustained individual mark
story.body: The club’s retrospective credits Hermosillo with three consecutive scoring crowns and 196 Cruz Azul goals. The 35-goal season was one part of that sustained record.

lessons.title: A final played through pain
lessons.subtitle: Hermosillo entered the 1997 final as a substitute and converted the decisive penalty.

story.title: The decisive moment
story.body: In extra time against León, goalkeeper Ángel Comizzo fouled Hermosillo. Despite a broken rib, the forward scored the penalty that delivered the eighth league title.

story.title: The match, in context
story.body: The episode is pinned to final opponent (León) and extra-time minute (99th minute), details that identify the competition and its turning point.

lessons.title: A continental hat-trick against Seattle
lessons.subtitle: Hermosillo’s goals helped Cruz Azul win the 1996 tournament edition.

story.title: Three in an 11–0 win
story.body: In the 1996 Concacaf Champions Cup, Cruz Azul routed the Seattle Sounders 11–0. Carlos Hermosillo scored three times in the group-stage match.

story.title: A separate chapter of his legacy
story.body: Concacaf’s historical account identifies Hermosillo among the two hat-trick scorers. This continental performance stands apart from his 1997 league-final penalty.

lessons.title: From the academy to the starting XI
lessons.subtitle: Óscar Pérez grew into Cruz Azul’s record-setting goalkeeper.

story.title: A homegrown debut
story.body: Pérez came through Cruz Azul’s academy and made his first-team debut on August 21, 1993. He stayed with the club through 2008.

story.title: A career in context
story.body: The timeline becomes concrete through first-team debut (August 21, 1993) and development (Cruz Azul youth academy). Those markers show how this chapter developed.

lessons.title: A Cruz Azul appearance record
lessons.subtitle: Pérez made more appearances for La Máquina than any other goalkeeper.

story.title: Four hundred and seventy
story.body: Across his Cruz Azul spell, the keeper played 470 matches. The club described him as its most-used goalkeeper.

story.title: The numbers behind the honor
story.body: The record is anchored by cruz azul matches (470) and club distinction (Most appearances by a club goalkeeper), which make the personal achievement precise.

lessons.title: Titles before and after the return
lessons.subtitle: Pérez was present for Cruz Azul trophies as both player and staff member.

story.title: A championship roster
story.body: He belonged to the 1996 and 1997 Concacaf-winning sides and the Invierno 1997 league champion. Later, he watched the 2021 Liga title from a coaching role.

story.title: The numbers behind the honor
story.body: The record is anchored by concacaf trophies (1996 and 1997) and league tournament (Invierno 1997), which make the personal achievement precise.

lessons.title: A late-career title and Hall of Fame induction
lessons.subtitle: Pérez won another league crown at 43 before his 2023 Hall of Fame induction.

story.title: A title at 43
story.body: After leaving Cruz Azul in 2008, Pérez continued with several clubs and won another league title with Pachuca at age 43.

story.title: An international recognition
story.body: On October 10, 2023, Pérez was inducted into the International Football Hall of Fame as part of its 2023 class.

lessons.title: The first league title
lessons.subtitle: A young Pumas side reached the top of Mexico in 1977.

story.title: A first star
story.body: After earlier cup success, Pumas won its first league championship in the 1976–77 season, beating Universidad de Guadalajara in the final.

story.title: The detail behind the milestone
story.body: The chronology is clearest in first league title season (1976–77) and final opponent (Universidad de Guadalajara), which anchor the wider story.

lessons.title: A season with three trophies
lessons.subtitle: The 1980–81 campaign brought domestic and international honors.

story.title: A triple celebration
story.body: Pumas won the league, the Concacaf club championship and the Copa Interamericana. Hugo Sánchez left for Spain after the season.

story.title: The detail behind the milestone
story.body: The chronology is clearest in league season (1980–81) and interamericana opponent (Nacional), which anchor the wider story.

lessons.title: The first short-tournament double
lessons.subtitle: Pumas became the first team to win consecutive short-format league titles.

story.title: Two titles in one year
story.body: Pumas won Clausura 2004 and Apertura 2004 under Hugo Sánchez. The second final, against Monterrey, completed the short-tournament bicampeonato.

story.title: The match, in context
story.body: The episode is pinned to tournament milestone (First short-tournament bicampeón) and second final opponent (Monterrey), details that identify the competition and its turning point.

lessons.title: From Pumas to the Bernabéu
lessons.subtitle: Sánchez carried his scoring career from Mexico into Spanish football.

story.title: A move to Madrid
story.body: After leaving Pumas for Spanish football, Hugo Sánchez joined Real Madrid from Atlético de Madrid in the summer of 1985.

story.title: An immediate impact
story.body: In his first season at the Bernabéu, he won the league and finished as its leading scorer with 22 goals.

lessons.title: A rare shared scoring crown
lessons.subtitle: Hugo and Cabinho made league history as teammates.

story.title: Twenty-six each
story.body: On June 2, 1979, Hugo scored his 26th goal of the season to draw level with Cabinho. They became the only teammates from one club to share the league’s scoring title.

story.title: The numbers behind the honor
story.body: The record is anchored by season goals (26) and co-winner (Cabinho), which make the personal achievement precise.

lessons.title: A century of Pumas goals
lessons.subtitle: The club’s league-and-liguilla list records Hugo’s scoring output.

story.title: Different competitions, different totals
story.body: Pumas’ October 2023 historical table credits Hugo Sánchez with 102 official club goals during his 1976–81 spell.

story.title: Reading the categories correctly
story.body: The table lists 97 in liga y liguilla: regular league and postseason combined. Five more came in other official tournaments. Those five are not a separate liguilla total.

lessons.title: A title-winning farewell
lessons.subtitle: Hugo’s final Pumas match before Europe came with a championship.

story.title: One last league match
story.body: Pumas beat Cruz Azul 4–1 on August 9, 1981. The club identifies the match as Hugo’s farewell before he left for Spain.

story.title: Why the chapter endures
story.body: The legacy rests on more than one moment: farewell date (August 9, 1981) and farewell opponent (Cruz Azul) place it in the club’s story.

lessons.title: A goalkeeper who could score
lessons.subtitle: Campos stretched the traditional role of a keeper.

story.title: A two-way player
story.body: Pumas described Campos as a goalkeeper-forward. He also led the 1990 Concacaf competition in scoring, a rare achievement for a goalkeeper.

story.title: A save on the world stage
story.body: At USA 1994, FIFA records Campos making a save in the 38th minute against Ireland.

lessons.title: A keeper wins the scoring race
lessons.subtitle: Campos was Concacaf’s top scorer while playing for Pumas.

story.title: Seven goals
story.body: Pumas beat Pinar del Río 3–1 on February 6, 1990, to claim the Concacaf title. Campos led the competition’s scoring with seven goals.

story.title: The numbers behind the honor
story.body: The record is anchored by competition goals (7) and title date (February 6, 1990), which make the personal achievement precise.

lessons.title: Three World Cup appearances
lessons.subtitle: Campos represented Mexico across three World Cup cycles.

story.title: A long international arc
story.body: Pumas’ retrospective identifies Campos with Mexico at the 1994, 1998 and 2002 World Cups. He was the only Pumas player in the club’s cited list to appear in all three.

story.title: A career in context
story.body: The timeline becomes concrete through first named world cup (USA 1994) and second edition (France 1998). Those markers show how this chapter developed.

lessons.title: A clean sheet before Mexico’s breakthrough
lessons.subtitle: Campos helped Mexico reach the 1999 Confederations Cup final.

story.title: A semifinal shutout
story.body: On August 1, 1999, Mexico beat the United States 1–0 in the FIFA Confederations Cup semifinal. Concacaf credits Jorge Campos with the clean sheet.

story.title: A step toward the title
story.body: Mexico then defeated Brazil 4–3 in the final to win its first FIFA tournament. Campos’ semifinal performance marked a different chapter from his 1990 club scoring record.

lessons.title: Back-to-back crowns after promotion
lessons.subtitle: León returned to the top flight and quickly became a champion again.

story.title: A return with momentum
story.body: León came back to the Primera División for 2012–13, then won the Apertura 2013 and Clausura 2014. Those consecutive league titles made the club a bicampeón.

story.title: A landmark season
story.body: The two championships followed a return from relegation in 2012. León’s 2013 title came against América; in 2014, the club beat Pachuca over two legs.

lessons.title: A first continental crown
lessons.subtitle: León turned a semifinal comeback into its first Concacaf title.

story.title: The road through Tigres
story.body: Fidel Ambriz scored early in the semifinal return leg, and Adonis Frías later supplied the series-winning goal. León advanced 4–3 on aggregate before facing LAFC.

story.title: The final in Los Angeles
story.body: Lucas Di Yorio scored in the second leg on June 4, 2023. León held on for a 3–1 aggregate victory and its first Concacaf championship.

lessons.title: Two finals, two different routes
lessons.subtitle: León’s domestic double run began with América and continued against Pachuca.

story.title: Ending a long wait
story.body: León’s Apertura 2013 victory ended a 21-year wait for a league title. The team beat América 5–1 on aggregate to take its sixth championship.

story.title: Following it with another title
story.body: In Clausura 2014, León defeated Pachuca 4–3 on aggregate to become bicampeón. The two final results mark the club’s return as a title-winning force.

lessons.title: A Chilean forward joins La Fiera
lessons.subtitle: Dávila arrived in León in 2020 and became a leading scorer.

story.title: A new chapter
story.body: Concacaf’s 2023 preview says Dávila joined León in 2020. By the time that article was published, he had scored 25 goals in 77 matches for the club.

story.title: A regular in continental play
story.body: He entered the 2023 Concacaf campaign after appearing in six earlier SCCL matches. The tournament gave him another stage to build his León record.

lessons.title: A quarterfinal brace
lessons.subtitle: Dávila’s goals helped León progress past Violette in 2023.

story.title: A five-goal first leg
story.body: León won the quarterfinal first leg 5–0, with Dávila scoring twice. The team finished the tie with a 6–2 aggregate win and reached its first SCCL semifinal.

story.title: A strong run
story.body: The two goals formed part of Dávila’s three-goal tournament total. He started five of León’s seven matches in the competition.

lessons.title: Best player in the 2023 Concacaf campaign
lessons.subtitle: Dávila’s seven-match run earned him the tournament’s top individual honor.

story.title: Three goals in seven
story.body: Dávila appeared in seven matches, started five and scored three goals during León’s 2023 Concacaf title run. He was selected as the tournament’s Best Player.

story.title: A team and individual breakthrough
story.body: León’s first continental title and Dávila’s Best Player Award came in the same campaign, linking his personal honor to the club’s first Concacaf crown.

lessons.title: A growing role at León
lessons.subtitle: A dated snapshot shows how the Chilean forward settled in.

story.title: A versatile contribution
story.body: Concacaf’s February 2023 profile described Dávila as a top performer at León, with goals and assists across club competitions.

story.title: Before the continental breakthrough
story.body: The same dated profile records four Liga MX assists in the previous year and six earlier SCCL appearances before the 2023 campaign.

lessons.title: From León academy to first team
lessons.subtitle: A homegrown player rose from the academy into senior football.

story.title: A long connection to León
story.body: In an interview shared by Concacaf, Ambriz said he joined Club León at age ten and made his first-team debut at sixteen.

story.title: Breaking into the senior side
story.body: By Concacaf’s 2023 profile, he had made more than 50 first-team league appearances and scored in four matches in the previous SCCL season.

lessons.title: A late header against Seattle
lessons.subtitle: Ambriz scored in the return leg of the 2022 continental quarterfinal.

story.title: A late equalizer
story.body: In the 2022 SCCL quarterfinal return leg, Ambriz headed home in the 91st minute against Seattle. The match ended 1–1, and Seattle advanced 4–1 on aggregate.

story.title: One goal, a different campaign
story.body: The late strike was a personal contribution in a separate Concacaf season from Ambriz’s 2023 youngest-scorer record.

lessons.title: The youngest scorer in the tournament
lessons.subtitle: His strike against Tigres set an age mark in the 2023 competition.

story.title: Twenty years and one month
story.body: Concacaf says Ambriz became the youngest scorer of the 2023 SCCL when he scored against Tigres, aged 20 years and one month.

story.title: A goal in the record campaign
story.body: The official tournament report credits Ambriz with one goal in the 2023 edition, the strike that established his age record.

lessons.title: The 2023 Young Player Award
lessons.subtitle: Ambriz’s breakthrough season earned a Concacaf individual honor.

story.title: Recognized among the best
story.body: Ambriz won Concacaf’s 2023 SCCL Best Young Player Award after a campaign in which he scored once.

story.title: A seven-match campaign
story.body: Concacaf’s Best XI report lists seven appearances and almost 92 percent pass completion for Ambriz.

lessons.title: A club begins by the Douro
lessons.subtitle: FC Porto dates its activity to September 1893.

story.title: A founding date
story.body: FC Porto’s statutes identify a precise day when the club was founded and began its activity.

story.title: A city club
story.body: The legal document anchors the institution in Porto and records its original name.

lessons.title: The back-heel that changed Porto
lessons.subtitle: A late equaliser set up a first European Cup triumph.

story.title: Bayern led
story.body: In the 1987 European Cup final, Bayern Munich were ahead 1–0 as time ran down.

story.title: A sudden reversal
story.body: Rabah Madjer back-heeled the equaliser, then set up Juary four minutes later.

lessons.title: Derlei decides it in Seville
lessons.subtitle: Porto’s 2003 UEFA Cup final went to extra time.

story.title: A pendulum final
story.body: Celtic twice came back to level the score after Porto took the lead.

story.title: Silver-goal finish
story.body: Derlei scored again in the 115th minute to give Porto its first UEFA Cup.

lessons.title: Deco finds his footing
lessons.subtitle: After loans and setbacks, Porto became his springboard.

story.title: A difficult start
story.body: UEFA’s career account says Deco could not establish himself at Benfica and went on loan to Alverca and Salgueiros.

story.title: A new level
story.body: At Porto he won three Portuguese league titles and two major European competitions.

lessons.title: Deco’s pass opens the final
lessons.subtitle: A disguised through ball helped Porto regain the lead against Celtic.

story.title: Porto were level
story.body: In the 2003 UEFA Cup final, Celtic had equalised Porto’s first goal early in the second half. Neil Lennon was marking Deco man to man, so movement helped him find space.

story.title: Deco sees the run
story.body: His angled outside-of-the-right-foot pass sent Dmitri Alenichev through for a 2–1 lead.

lessons.title: A debut goal against Brazil
lessons.subtitle: Deco’s first Portugal appearance came against the country where he was born.

story.title: A new international shirt
story.body: Deco, born in Brazil, became a Portuguese citizen and was called up for Portugal in 2003.

story.title: An immediate impact
story.body: He came on as a substitute and scored a late free-kick winner against Brazil.

lessons.title: Deco’s European awards double
lessons.subtitle: UEFA named him both its best midfielder and overall MVP for 2003/04.

story.title: A remarkable season
story.body: Deco helped Porto win the Champions League and was honoured at UEFA’s 2004 awards.

story.title: Two distinctions
story.body: He received both the Best Midfielder award and Most Valuable Player award.

lessons.title: A long career in goal
lessons.subtitle: Baía’s career brought success in Portugal and Spain.

story.title: Two Porto spells
story.body: UEFA reports that Baía made 406 league appearances for Porto across two spells.

story.title: A wide honours list
story.body: He won club trophies in Portugal and Spain and earned 80 caps for Portugal.

lessons.title: Baía shuts the door on Monaco
lessons.subtitle: His early intervention helped Porto through a tense final.

story.title: A dangerous break
story.body: Monaco captain Ludovic Giuly broke through in the opening minutes of the 2004 final.

story.title: Baía reads it
story.body: The Porto goalkeeper rushed out and made a sliding challenge before Giuly could finish.

lessons.title: A rare set of three European cups
lessons.subtitle: Baía completed a continental trophy treble with Porto in 2004.

story.title: Different competitions
story.body: He won the Cup Winners’ Cup with Barcelona before collecting the UEFA Cup with Porto.

story.title: The final piece
story.body: Porto’s 2004 Champions League victory completed the set. By retirement in 2007, his domestic collection also included eight Portuguese Super Cups.

lessons.title: A keeper decorated across leagues
lessons.subtitle: Baía collected honours in Portugal and Spain and a UEFA award.

story.title: A Portuguese collection
story.body: UEFA’s career tally includes ten league titles, five domestic cups and eight Portuguese Super Cups.

story.title: Recognition as a goalkeeper
story.body: In 2004, UEFA’s European awards named Baía its Best Goalkeeper.

lessons.title: An ambitious club takes shape
lessons.subtitle: José Alvalade imagined Sporting as a major European club.

story.title: A breakaway in 1906
story.body: The club history says Alvalade and supporters left Campo Grande Foot-Ball Club over its social direction.

story.title: A broad sporting idea
story.body: Sporting began with five sports, not only football.

lessons.title: Sporting wins after a replay
lessons.subtitle: João Morais’s corner settled the 1964 Cup Winners’ Cup final replay.

story.title: One draw was not enough
story.body: Sporting and MTK Budapest drew 3–3 after extra time in Brussels.

story.title: A direct finish
story.body: In Antwerp two days later, Morais scored directly from a corner in the 1–0 win.

lessons.title: A final played at home
lessons.subtitle: Sporting led the 2005 UEFA Cup final at half-time before CSKA turned it around.

story.title: Rogério strikes first
story.body: Sporting’s official history says Rogério gave the hosts a 1–0 lead before the interval.

story.title: CSKA rallies
story.body: The Russian side scored three second-half goals to win 3–1 at José Alvalade.

lessons.title: A first-team door opens
lessons.subtitle: Ronaldo’s Sporting debut came at 17 in a European qualifier.

story.title: A teenager earns his chance
story.body: Sporting used Ronaldo in its Champions League qualifier against Inter.

story.title: The first senior appearance
story.body: He entered in the second half of the 0–0 first leg on 14 August 2002.

lessons.title: A goal before the debut
lessons.subtitle: Ronaldo scored his first Sporting goal in a pre-season friendly against Betis.

story.title: A glimpse in pre-season
story.body: UEFA recalls his goal came in a 3–2 friendly victory shortly before the Inter qualifier.

story.title: A difficult angle
story.body: He beat the goalkeeper and curled the ball into the top corner from outside the area.

lessons.title: The Sporting audition in Manchester
lessons.subtitle: A friendly against United helped trigger Ronaldo’s transfer.

story.title: A preseason showcase
story.body: Sporting played Manchester United in a friendly in August 2003.

story.title: A transfer follows
story.body: UEFA records that United completed Ronaldo’s signing days later, for €17.5 million.

lessons.title: Five Champions League wins by 2018
lessons.subtitle: Ronaldo became the first player to reach five titles.

story.title: A first medal at United
story.body: Ronaldo began his collection with Manchester United in 2008.

story.title: A new milestone in Kyiv
story.body: After Real Madrid beat Liverpool 3–1 in the 2018 final, he became the first player to win five Champions League finals.

lessons.title: Six seasons before Spain
lessons.subtitle: Figo’s Sporting years launched an illustrious club and international career.

story.title: A youth international
story.body: UEFA highlights his 1989 European Under-16 title with Portugal.

story.title: A first club cup
story.body: He spent six years at Sporting and won the 1995 Portuguese Cup before moving to Barcelona.

lessons.title: A Sporting debut and farewell
lessons.subtitle: Figo’s first-team debut and final appearance for Sporting both came against Marítimo.

story.title: First appearance
story.body: Sporting records Figo’s first-team debut on 1 April 1990 against Marítimo.

story.title: A final cup match
story.body: Five years later, his Sporting farewell also came against Marítimo in the Portuguese Cup final.

lessons.title: Portugal’s comeback against England
lessons.subtitle: Figo helped spark a 3–2 EURO 2000 comeback after England scored twice.

story.title: A difficult start
story.body: Portugal fell 2–0 behind in its opening group match against England.

story.title: Figo responds
story.body: His long-range strike pulled one back, and Portugal went on to win 3–2.

lessons.title: A record for Portugal
lessons.subtitle: Figo’s international career ended with a national appearance record.

story.title: Fifteen years
story.body: UEFA describes Figo as a Portugal mainstay for 15 years.

story.title: A record total
story.body: He finished with 127 caps, then a record for the national team.

lessons.title: Werder’s long Bundesliga story
lessons.subtitle: A founding member, an early champion and a four-time winner

story.title: A founding member
story.body: Werder qualified as one of the northern Oberliga representatives when the Bundesliga began in 1963. It finished tenth in that first season.

story.title: Early success and returns
story.body: The club won its first Bundesliga title in 1964/65 and ultimately collected four. After relegations in 1980 and 2021, Werder returned immediately each time.

lessons.title: Allofs and Rufer seal a European cup
lessons.subtitle: Werder beat Monaco 2–0 in the 1992 final

story.title: A final in Lisbon
story.body: On 6 May 1992, Werder Bremen met AS Monaco at Lisbon’s Estádio da Luz in the Cup Winners’ Cup final.

story.title: Two goals, one trophy
story.body: Klaus Allofs opened the scoring before Wynton Rufer doubled Werder’s lead in the second half. The 2–0 win secured the European trophy.

lessons.title: Özil decides the 2009 DFB Cup final
lessons.subtitle: Werder beat Leverkusen to lift the club’s sixth cup

story.title: A second trophy that decade
story.body: Five years after the domestic double, Werder reached the 2009 DFB Cup final against Bayer Leverkusen.

story.title: One goal was enough
story.body: Mesut Özil scored the only goal in the final, completing a cup run that followed a dramatic semi-final win over Hamburg.

lessons.title: A club formed through Hamburg’s football history
lessons.subtitle: Several Hamburg predecessors came together under the HSV name

story.title: Roots before the name
story.body: HSV’s current official foundation year is 1887, taken from SC Germania; the modern club’s predecessor organizations joined across 1914 and 1919.

story.title: A decorated German club
story.body: Hamburg won national championships before the Bundesliga, became a founding member in 1963, and later built a European-winning era.

lessons.title: Seeler and the 1960 championship final
lessons.subtitle: HSV edged Cologne 3–2 to win a third national title

story.title: A decisive final
story.body: The club dates the final to 25 June 1960, when HSV faced 1. FC Köln for the German championship.

story.title: Homegrown strength
story.body: Seven HSV players came from the club’s youth ranks in the 3–2 victory; Uwe Seeler was later named Germany’s first Footballer of the Year.

lessons.title: Magath’s shot puts Hamburg on Europe’s throne
lessons.subtitle: HSV beat Juventus in the 1983 European Cup final in Athens

story.title: The European Cup final
story.body: Hamburg met Juventus on 25 May 1983 at Athens’ Olympic Stadium.

story.title: One early strike
story.body: Felix Magath scored in the ninth minute. HSV held on for a 1–0 win and its first European Cup title.

lessons.title: From Lima to repeated returns to Bremen
lessons.subtitle: Pizarro’s German career began at Werder and repeatedly brought him back

story.title: First move to Germany
story.body: Claudio Pizarro left Alianza Lima for Werder Bremen in 1999, aged 20. Two seasons and 29 Bundesliga goals later, Bayern signed him.

story.title: A long route back
story.body: After Chelsea, he returned to Werder in 2008, later moved through Bayern and Cologne, then finished his career in Bremen in 2020.

lessons.title: Pizarro extends the age record at 40
lessons.subtitle: A late winner in Bremen carried his Bundesliga longevity record further

story.title: The first record
story.body: Pizarro first became the Bundesliga’s oldest goalscorer with a late equaliser against Hertha in February 2019, aged 40 years and 136 days.

story.title: A record extended
story.body: On 18 May, his 88th-minute winner against Leipzig extended the record: Pizarro was 40 years and 227 days old.

lessons.title: A Bundesliga record scorer for Werder
lessons.subtitle: Four Bremen spells brought Pizarro 109 league goals

story.title: The club’s leading Bundesliga scorer
story.body: Werder’s official record table lists Pizarro first with 109 league goals, ahead of Marco Bode on 101.

story.title: A durable scoring career
story.body: Across the Bundesliga, Pizarro scored in 21 consecutive calendar years and appeared in 490 matches, then a foreign-player appearance record.

lessons.title: Six Bundesliga titles and a European treble
lessons.subtitle: Pizarro collected major honors across Bayern and Werder spells

story.title: Trophy years
story.body: Pizarro won six Bundesliga titles, all with Bayern, and lifted the DFB Cup six times, including once with Werder.

story.title: A continental first
story.body: In 2012/13 he completed Bayern’s Bundesliga, DFB Cup and Champions League treble and became the first Peruvian to win the European Cup.

lessons.title: From Kaiserslautern to the Weser
lessons.subtitle: Klose developed into a leading Bundesliga scorer at Werder

story.title: A route through the German tiers
story.body: Klose moved through FC 08 Homburg before reaching Kaiserslautern, where he made his Bundesliga breakthrough.

story.title: A Bremen peak
story.body: After joining Werder in 2004, he scored 53 goals in 89 league matches and moved to Bayern after three seasons.

lessons.title: Klose’s volley in a 6–0 Werder win
lessons.subtitle: A brace and a left-footed volley stood out against Cologne

story.title: A big result late in the season
story.body: On the penultimate matchday of 2005/06, Werder overwhelmed Cologne 6–0; Klose and two teammates each scored twice.

story.title: The goal that stood out
story.body: Klose’s second goal made it 2–0: after a deflection from Lukas Podolski, he struck the dropping ball left-footed into the upper-right corner.

lessons.title: A scoring crown at Bremen
lessons.subtitle: Klose’s 2005/06 Bundesliga season produced 25 goals

story.title: A league-leading season
story.body: Klose scored 25 goals in 26 Bundesliga appearances for Werder in 2005/06 and won the scoring crown.

story.title: More than finishing
story.body: Across the 2005/06 and 2006/07 seasons, he also led the Bundesliga in assists with 28 combined.

lessons.title: A World Cup winner from Werder’s attack
lessons.subtitle: Klose paired German honors with a club-player award

story.title: A fan-voted distinction
story.body: Werder museum visitors chose Klose as their Player of the Season for 2005/06, giving him 45.68% of the vote.

story.title: A later career peak
story.body: With Germany, he won the 2014 World Cup, the defining international title of his playing career.

lessons.title: A teenager begins the Seeler era
lessons.subtitle: Uwe Seeler debuted for HSV at 16 and scored immediately

story.title: First team at sixteen
story.body: HSV’s history dates Seeler’s first appearance to August 1953, when he was only 16.

story.title: A goal from the start
story.body: He opened his Oberliga Nord account in his debut and soon made his Germany debut.

lessons.title: A hat-trick in the first DFB Cup triumph
lessons.subtitle: Seeler scored all three goals against Dortmund in 1963

story.title: A first cup
story.body: Just days before the Bundesliga began in 1963, HSV met Borussia Dortmund in the DFB Cup final.

story.title: Seeler decides it
story.body: Uwe Seeler scored a hat-trick in the 3–0 win, sealing the first DFB Cup in the club’s history.

lessons.title: The Bundesliga’s first scoring champion
lessons.subtitle: Seeler scored 30 in the league’s first season

story.title: A first scoring crown
story.body: In 1963/64, the first Bundesliga season, Seeler became its first top scorer with 30 goals in 30 matches.

story.title: HSV’s leading league scorer
story.body: He finished with 137 Bundesliga goals for Hamburg, a club record in the league.

lessons.title: A loyal career crowned in Hamburg
lessons.subtitle: Seeler won club honors and seven northern scoring crowns

story.title: A long HSV career
story.body: Seeler played his entire senior club career with Hamburg and retired in 1972 after his farewell match at Volksparkstadion.

story.title: Individual honors
story.body: HSV credits him with seven northern scoring titles and three Germany Footballer of the Year awards.

lessons.title: Liverpool star makes a new start in Hamburg
lessons.subtitle: Keegan’s path took him from Scunthorpe through Liverpool to HSV

story.title: A different challenge
story.body: After five seasons at Scunthorpe and six at Liverpool, Keegan left England in 1977 for Hamburg.

story.title: Three years with HSV
story.body: The club profile records 90 league appearances and 32 goals in Hamburg before his 1980 return to England with Southampton.

lessons.title: A championship season in Hamburg
lessons.subtitle: Keegan scored 17 league goals as HSV won the 1978/79 title

story.title: A stronger second season
story.body: After 12 Bundesliga goals in his first campaign, Keegan found his rhythm under new coach Branko Zebec.

story.title: Title and individual honor
story.body: His 17 goals helped HSV win its first Bundesliga title, and Keegan collected the European Footballer of the Year award for a second straight year.

lessons.title: A European final after a famous comeback
lessons.subtitle: Hamburg erased a two-goal deficit to reach the European Cup final

story.title: A semi-final surge
story.body: After a 2–0 defeat in Madrid, HSV overturned the semi-final against Real Madrid with a 5–1 home win; Caspar Memering scored the late goal that completed the comeback.

story.title: One step short
story.body: Keegan stayed for a final attempt at European glory, but Nottingham Forest beat Hamburg at the Bernabéu before he returned to England.

lessons.title: European honors and a Hamburg scoring record
lessons.subtitle: Two Ballon d’Ors and 90 Bundesliga appearances for HSV

story.title: Consecutive European honors
story.body: While at HSV, Keegan won the Ballon d’Or in 1978 and 1979, the European Footballer of the Year award in consecutive years.

story.title: A three-year spell
story.body: Across his 1977–1980 Hamburg spell, Keegan made 90 Bundesliga appearances and scored 32 league goals. These are league totals, rather than totals across every competition.

lessons.title: Freiburg’s leap into Europe
lessons.subtitle: A second Bundesliga season became an unexpected springboard to Europe.

story.title: A remarkable second season
story.body: After securing Bundesliga survival in 1994, Freiburg finished third the following year. The club’s early top-flight campaign quickly became a European breakthrough.

story.title: A first continental step
story.body: The 1994/95 finish was only three points behind champions Borussia Dortmund and earned Freiburg its first European competition place.

lessons.title: A first cup final
lessons.subtitle: A 3–1 semifinal win over Hamburg took Freiburg to Berlin for the first time.

story.title: Three goals before the final
story.body: On April 19, 2022, Freiburg defeated Hamburg 3–1 in the DFB-Pokal semifinal. Nils Petersen, Nicolas Höfler and Vincenzo Grifo scored.

story.title: A new stage for the club
story.body: That result sent Freiburg to the first DFB-Pokal final in its history, scheduled for May 21 in Berlin.

lessons.title: Freiburg’s first cup final
lessons.subtitle: The 2022 final went through extra time and penalties before Leipzig lifted the trophy.

story.title: A breakthrough in Berlin
story.body: Freiburg’s first DFB-Pokal final was level at 1–1 after normal time. Maximilian Eggestein had put the side ahead in the 19th minute.

story.title: A painful shootout
story.body: RB Leipzig won the penalty shootout. Freiburg hit the woodwork four times, and captain Christian Günter sent his penalty over the bar.

lessons.title: Back in the Bundesliga
lessons.subtitle: After two seasons away, Mainz returned to the top flight in 2009 under Jörn Andersen.

story.title: A second promotion
story.body: Mainz secured its second Bundesliga promotion on May 24, 2009, with a 4–0 win over Rot-Weiß Oberhausen.

story.title: A composed finish
story.body: The side ended the campaign second with 63 points, returning after two years in the second division.

lessons.title: The first Bundesliga win
lessons.subtitle: Mainz answered its opening-day loss by overturning a halftime deficit against Hamburg.

story.title: A response at Bruchweg
story.body: A week after losing its first Bundesliga match, Mainz hosted Hamburger SV and fell behind before the break.

story.title: Da Silva turns it around
story.body: Antonio da Silva scored twice to give Mainz its first Bundesliga victory, turning the home ground into a celebration.

lessons.title: Mainz steps onto Europe’s stage
lessons.subtitle: A Fair Play place opened the club’s first UEFA Cup tie in 2005.

story.title: A first European night
story.body: Mainz entered the UEFA Cup through the Fair Play ranking and hosted Mika Ashtarak in its first European match.

story.title: An emphatic start
story.body: The 4–0 win took place in Frankfurt because UEFA required all-seater seating for European fixtures at Bruchweg.

lessons.title: A striker finds his home in Freiburg
lessons.subtitle: After several German clubs, Petersen arrived on loan and chose to stay after relegation.

story.title: A route through Germany
story.body: Petersen played for Carl Zeiss Jena, Energie Cottbus, Bayern Munich and Werder Bremen before joining Freiburg.

story.title: Staying through a setback
story.body: He arrived on loan in the winter of 2014/15. When Freiburg dropped to the second division, he chose to remain in the Black Forest.

lessons.title: A final home goal
lessons.subtitle: Petersen scored in his last home appearance, five minutes after entering against Wolfsburg.

story.title: One last entrance
story.body: On May 19, 2023, Petersen came off the bench in his final home game for Freiburg against Wolfsburg.

story.title: A goodbye in the 75th minute
story.body: He tapped home in the 75th minute, helping Freiburg win 2–0 and giving supporters a final goal to celebrate.

lessons.title: A Freiburg scoring record
lessons.subtitle: At his 2023 farewell, Petersen left with 105 goals in 277 competitive appearances for the club.

story.title: A complete Freiburg tally
story.body: Petersen made 277 competitive appearances for Freiburg and scored 105 times.

story.title: The assist total
story.body: He also supplied 21 assists across those appearances, while retaining the Bundesliga substitute-scoring record.

lessons.title: Silver in Rio
lessons.subtitle: Petersen shared Germany’s tournament scoring lead before the Olympic final ended on penalties.

story.title: A medal run
story.body: Petersen won silver with Germany at the 2016 Olympics in Rio. He scored six times during the men’s tournament.

story.title: A tense final
story.body: The final against Brazil finished 1–1 before penalties. Petersen missed his attempt, and Brazil won the shootout.

lessons.title: The Freiburg return becomes permanent
lessons.subtitle: Grifo’s first spell led to moves away, a loan return and a permanent home in 2019.

story.title: A first Freiburg spell
story.body: Grifo joined Freiburg from Hoffenheim in 2015, then moved to Borussia Mönchengladbach in 2017 and returned to Hoffenheim a year later.

story.title: Back to Breisgau
story.body: He returned on loan in January 2019. Freiburg made the move permanent that summer.

lessons.title: Three goals in twenty minutes
lessons.subtitle: Grifo’s hat-trick drove Freiburg’s 4–1 win over Union Berlin in November 2022.

story.title: A lightning start
story.body: On November 13, 2022, Grifo scored from the penalty spot in the fourth minute, then added a second in the sixth.

story.title: A hat-trick by the twentieth
story.body: He converted another penalty in the 20th minute. Freiburg beat Union Berlin 4–1 and went into the winter break second.

lessons.title: A new Freiburg scoring benchmark
lessons.subtitle: On March 7, 2026, Grifo reached 105 club goals and matched Nils Petersen’s record.

story.title: An equal mark
story.body: Grifo’s 34th-minute goal against Leverkusen was his 105th for Freiburg, matching Petersen’s club scoring total.

story.title: A dated snapshot
story.body: The Bundesliga’s report counted 344 competitive appearances and 91 assists for Grifo at that milestone.

lessons.title: A promotion-winning debut season
lessons.subtitle: Grifo helped Freiburg win the 2015/16 second division and returned the club to the Bundesliga.

story.title: A title in year one
story.body: Freiburg won the 2. Bundesliga in Grifo’s first season with the club, earning promotion.

story.title: A productive campaign
story.body: In that division, Grifo played 31 matches and recorded 14 goals and 15 assists.

lessons.title: A decade on the pitch
lessons.subtitle: Klopp’s Mainz playing years began before he later moved from the pitch to the coaching bench.

story.title: A move to the Bruchweg
story.body: Klopp began his Mainz playing tenure in 1990 and became a long-serving part of the squad.

story.title: A long playing spell
story.body: His playing spell ended in 2001, when his role at the club changed from player to coach.

lessons.title: A player becomes the coach
lessons.subtitle: An injury interrupted Klopp’s playing career and Mainz promoted him from within in February 2001.

story.title: An unexpected appointment
story.body: On February 27, 2001, Mainz turned to Klopp, an injured right-back, after dismissing Eckhard Krautzun.

story.title: A fast first response
story.body: His first match in charge ended in a 1–0 win over MSV Duisburg, with Christof Babatz scoring the winner.

lessons.title: A dual Mainz tally
lessons.subtitle: The club’s 2026 profile counted Klopp’s playing and coaching work separately.

story.title: The player’s totals
story.body: Klopp made 340 competitive appearances as a Mainz player and scored 56 goals.

story.title: The coach’s total
story.body: He later coached the club in 270 matches, according to Mainz’s 2026 retrospective.

lessons.title: The third attempt reaches the Bundesliga
lessons.subtitle: Klopp led Mainz to its first Bundesliga promotion after two near misses.

story.title: A decisive final day
story.body: On May 23, 2004, Mainz defeated Eintracht Trier 3–0 to secure its first Bundesliga promotion.

story.title: Thurk delivers
story.body: Michael Thurk scored twice in the final match, helping Klopp’s side reach the top flight on 54 points.

lessons.title: From academy to senior football
lessons.subtitle: Bell’s youth development, loan years and early top-flight run formed a steady route into Mainz’s defence.

story.title: A homegrown route
story.body: Bell joined Mainz’s academy in 2007 as a 15-year-old. Loan spells at 1860 Munich and Eintracht Frankfurt came before his return.

story.title: A first-team opening
story.body: Under Thomas Tuchel, Bell made 35 Bundesliga appearances between December 2012 and summer 2014, building from his loan development into the senior side.

lessons.title: Back after myocarditis
lessons.subtitle: Bell returned after months away from football and began rebuilding his match rhythm.

story.title: A difficult absence
story.body: Myocarditis kept Bell out of action for about four months. His Bundesliga return followed a 262-day gap from his previous top-flight appearance.

story.title: Back in the squad
story.body: He returned in a DFB-Pokal match at SV Wehen Wiesbaden, then appeared against Union Berlin for his 267th Bundesliga game.

lessons.title: A 300th Bundesliga appearance
lessons.subtitle: Bell reached his milestone in a 2–1 Mainz win away at Leipzig in 2026.

story.title: A rare mark
story.body: Bell’s appearance at RB Leipzig was his 300th Bundesliga game for Mainz, a milestone reached after more than thirteen years in the top flight.

story.title: A winning occasion
story.body: Mainz won the match 2–1, making the record appearance part of an important away result.

lessons.title: A youth title with a personal setback
lessons.subtitle: Bell helped Mainz’s U19 win the 2009 national championship, despite missing the final injured.

story.title: A team achievement
story.body: At 17, Bell was part of the Mainz U19 side that won Germany’s A-Junioren championship in 2009.

story.title: Contribution beyond the final
story.body: He had started 25 league matches on the way to the title, but an injury kept him out of the 2–1 final against Borussia Dortmund.

lessons.title: From Philips Elftal to PSV
lessons.subtitle: A factory team became a wider sports association.

story.title: A workplace team
story.body: Philips employees formed the Philips Elftal in 1910, before the association PSV formally existed.

story.title: A shared beginning
story.body: The team played its first match at the site that became Philips Stadion, then joined the wider association in 1913.

lessons.title: A shootout crowns a golden season
lessons.subtitle: PSV won the 1988 European Cup after a goalless final.

story.title: A tense final
story.body: PSV and Benfica could not score in normal time or extra time in Stuttgart.

story.title: One save decides it
story.body: Hans van Breukelen stopped António Veloso’s kick as PSV won the shootout and completed a treble season.

lessons.title: PSV break through in Europe
lessons.subtitle: A 3–0 home win settled the 1978 UEFA Cup final.

story.title: A stalemate in Corsica
story.body: The first leg against Bastia ended goalless.

story.title: Three goals at home
story.body: PSV scored three in the return, with Willy van de Kerkhof opening the scoring and René van de Kerkhof adding the third.

lessons.title: Ruud’s scoring years in Eindhoven
lessons.subtitle: From a teenage professional debut to the Eredivisie scoring crown.

story.title: An early professional start
story.body: Van Nistelrooij made his professional debut for FC Den Bosch at 17 in 1993/94. After four seasons there and one at Heerenveen, he joined PSV in 1998.

story.title: A league scoring crown
story.body: In his first PSV season, 1998/99, he scored 31 Eredivisie goals and finished as the league’s leading scorer. This total describes that league season, rather than all competitions or his entire career.

lessons.title: Van Nistelrooij turns the Ajax match
lessons.subtitle: After the break, his goal put PSV ahead in a 3–1 win.

story.title: A response after half-time
story.body: PSV trailed Ajax 0–1 at the interval on 4 April 1999.

story.title: A decisive finish
story.body: Luc Nilis equalised; Van Nistelrooij then scored the second before Nilis completed the 3–1 win.

lessons.title: Four goals in one European night
lessons.subtitle: On 3 November 2004, he scored every United goal against Sparta Praha.

story.title: A record-equalling night
story.body: Manchester United beat Sparta Praha 4–1 in the Champions League.

story.title: One scorer, four finishes
story.body: Van Nistelrooij scored all four, matching the competition’s then-record for goals by one player in a match. Liam Miller’s late cut-back set up the fourth.

lessons.title: A 12-goal Champions League season
lessons.subtitle: Van Nistelrooij finished top scorer in 2002/03.

story.title: A campaign-leading total
story.body: UEFA’s season table lists Van Nistelrooij first among the 2002/03 top scorers.

story.title: A personal benchmark
story.body: His 12 goals led the chart ahead of Filippo Inzaghi’s 10.

lessons.title: Robben’s two seasons at PSV
lessons.subtitle: The winger joined at 18 and recorded 17 league goals.

story.title: A young arrival
story.body: Robben moved from Groningen to PSV in 2002, aged 18.

story.title: A short, productive spell
story.body: PSV records 56 league appearances and 17 league goals from 2002 through 2004.

lessons.title: Robben takes the winning kick
lessons.subtitle: His penalty sent the Netherlands into the EURO 2004 semi-finals.

story.title: A goalless 120 minutes
story.body: The Netherlands and Sweden could not be separated in their quarter-final.

story.title: The final kick
story.body: Robben converted the winning penalty as the Netherlands advanced 5–4 in the shootout. He beat Sweden goalkeeper Andreas Isaksson.

lessons.title: A saved penalty in Munich
lessons.subtitle: Petr Čech denied Robben in extra time of the 2012 final.

story.title: A chance in extra time
story.body: With the 2012 Champions League final level at 1–1, Bayern had a chance to regain the lead.

story.title: Čech makes the save
story.body: Robben took the penalty early in extra time, but Petr Čech saved it; Chelsea later won the shootout 4–3.

lessons.title: A century of UEFA club appearances
lessons.subtitle: Robben reached 100 UEFA club matches in April 2017.

story.title: A long European career
story.body: UEFA records his century in its club competitions during Bayern’s 2017 quarter-final against Real Madrid.

story.title: A dated milestone
story.body: The milestone came in the first leg; Robben later scored twice in his final Champions League appearance.

lessons.title: From Wilhelmina to Feijenoord
lessons.subtitle: A Rotterdam club’s name and colours settled in 1912.

story.title: A café beginning
story.body: Four young men formed Wilhelmina at café De Vereeniging in 1908.

story.title: A lasting identity
story.body: The club took the permanent name Rotterdamsche Voetbal Vereeniging Feijenoord in 1912 and adopted its red-and-white shirt.

lessons.title: Kindvall wins the European Cup
lessons.subtitle: Feyenoord beat Celtic after extra time in Milan.

story.title: A Dutch first
story.body: Feyenoord became the first Dutch club to win the European Cup.

story.title: A late finish
story.body: Ove Kindvall scored the extra-time winner against Celtic on 6 May 1970.

lessons.title: A European Cup lifted at De Kuip
lessons.subtitle: Feyenoord edged Dortmund 3–2 in the 2002 UEFA Cup final.

story.title: The home final
story.body: Feyenoord hosted Borussia Dortmund at De Kuip on 8 May 2002.

story.title: A match of swings
story.body: Van Hooijdonk scored twice; Tomasson’s goal proved decisive after Dortmund twice reduced the margin.

lessons.title: A long route back to Rotterdam
lessons.subtitle: Kuyt’s 19-season career ended where his Feyenoord story began.

story.title: Clubs across a career
story.body: The KNVB traces his path from Quick Boys through Utrecht and Feyenoord to Liverpool and Fenerbahçe, before his return.

story.title: A long international run
story.body: He finished with 104 Netherlands caps and 24 goals.

lessons.title: A hat-trick on the title day
lessons.subtitle: Kuyt’s three goals secured Feyenoord’s first league title since 1999.

story.title: One match left
story.body: On 14 May 2017, Feyenoord needed a result against Heracles to confirm the championship.

story.title: Captain delivers
story.body: Kuyt scored a hat-trick in the 3–1 win, ending the club’s 18-year wait for the league title.

lessons.title: Kuyt scores in the 2007 final
lessons.subtitle: His late goal gave Liverpool a brief route back into the match.

story.title: A late response
story.body: Milan led Liverpool 2–0 in Athens before Kuyt headed in Daniel Agger’s flick-on from a corner late in normal time.

story.title: No second comeback
story.body: Liverpool finished the 2007 final behind 2–1; Kuyt’s goal was too late to force extra time.

lessons.title: Caps and goals for the Netherlands
lessons.subtitle: At retirement, Kuyt had 104 caps and 24 international goals.

story.title: A regular for Oranje
story.body: Kuyt made 104 senior Netherlands appearances and scored 24 goals.

story.title: Two personal totals
story.body: The KNVB records 104 appearances and 24 goals for the Netherlands.

lessons.title: From Feyenoord prospect to cup winner
lessons.subtitle: Van Persie rose through Feyenoord before moving to Arsenal.

story.title: A breakthrough in Rotterdam
story.body: UEFA described the 20-year-old as a regular after two seasons in Feyenoord’s first team.

story.title: A European honour
story.body: He helped Feyenoord win the 2002 UEFA Cup and was named Dutch Young Footballer of the Year that season.

lessons.title: An 18-year-old earns his place in a final
lessons.subtitle: Van Persie helped Feyenoord beat Dortmund in the 2002 UEFA Cup final.

story.title: A young starter
story.body: At 18, Van Persie started on the left for Feyenoord in the final against Borussia Dortmund.

story.title: A run creates danger
story.body: UEFA notes he won the free kick for Feyenoord’s second goal with a driving run away from Márcio Amoroso.

lessons.title: The header that changed the Spain match
lessons.subtitle: Van Persie levelled just before half-time in the 2014 World Cup.

story.title: A response to Spain
story.body: After Spain took the lead, Van Persie met Daley Blind’s long cross with a leaping header.

story.title: A momentum shift
story.body: The goal made it 1–1 before the break; the Netherlands went on to win 5–1.

lessons.title: A record and a Golden Boot season
lessons.subtitle: His 2011/12 league campaign and 2013 international hat-trick set personal marks.

story.title: A prolific league season
story.body: Van Persie scored 30 Premier League goals for Arsenal in 2011/12, winning the Golden Boot.

story.title: A national record
story.body: In October 2013, his hat-trick against Hungary took him to 41 Netherlands goals, then a national record.
